newsitem.title: JAPAN: Failed Hanwa Bank objects to MOF liquidation plan.
newsitem.headline: Failed Hanwa Bank objects to MOF liquidation plan.

text.p: Hanwa Bank Ltd, which collapsed last November, filed an objection on Monday to a liquidation scheme worked out by Japan's Finance Ministry (MOF), a senior MOF official said.

"We will thoroughly consider the content of the objection that has been submitted to us and will deal with it appropriately according to the law," Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference.
He said the objection was delivered to MOF's Osaka office around noon on Monday.
Hanwa Bank sources told Reuters that there were unresolved issues with the MOF liquidation scheme regarding guarantees of job security for the bank's 850 employees.
MOF announced last November that it had suspended operations at the second-tier regional bank, except for deposit withdrawals, because it was unable to recover bad loans.
Finance Ministry officials said a new bank would be set up for the sole purpose of winding up Hanwa's business.
